summary: Suggests several updates to the Reliable Data Protocol specified in RFC 908, based on experience. This revised version is experimental.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1151 proposes fixes to the Reliable Data Protocol based on experiments. It changes the header and corrects ambiguities in the earlier specification.

questions: what changes did rfc 1151 make to rdp
subtitle: Updates RDP with a new checksum, larger ports and corrections to RFC 908.

tldr.problem: Experiments found ambiguities and problems in the Reliable Data Protocol specification in RFC 908.
tldr.mechanism: RDP version 2 changes the checksum, increases port size to 16 bits and corrects several state-machine and window descriptions.
tldr.outcome: The revised protocol is experimental; the RFC says demand for RDP implementations was limited.

today: RFC 1151 is an Experimental update to RFC 908. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why RDP Was Revised
sections.content:
Experiments in 1986 and 1987 revealed ambiguities and problems in the RDP specification in RFC 908. The authors had hoped to revise the complete specification, but say limited demand for RDP implementations made that effort difficult to justify.

This RFC lists changes the authors consider appropriate for version 2. The revised protocol is identified as experimental.
sections.plainLanguage: The experiments found unclear or inconsistent parts of the earlier RDP specification. This RFC lists proposed corrections and header changes.

sections.title: Changes to the Header
sections.content:
The header changes are a new checksum algorithm, an increase in port size and an incremented version number. RDP now uses the 16-bit TCP checksum specified in RFC 793; the authors say checksum performance varied substantially across comparable hardware.

Ports grow from 8 bits to 16 bits. Port numbers below 1024 are reserved for well-defined applications, and allocable ports begin at 1024. The version number becomes 2.
sections.plainLanguage: The new version uses a 16-bit checksum and 16-bit port numbers. Its version field is set to 2.

sections.title: Corrections and Remaining Flow-Control Issue
sections.content:
The RFC corrects inconsistencies in the pseudo-code for SND.UNA, SYN-SENT, SYN-RCVD, CLOSED and CLOSE-WAIT states. It clarifies acknowledgement handling and says the right edge of the window is outside the window.

It also notes that RDP flow control does not let a receiver close the sender's window. A suggested approach is to acknowledge a segment only after delivering it to the application, but the RFC says this approach has not been tested. Security issues are not addressed.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC corrects state and window descriptions. It also identifies a flow-control problem and an untested possible solution.

references.text: Velten, D., Hinden, R., and J. Sax, "Reliable Data Protocol", RFC 908, July 1984.
Postel, J., "Transmission Control Protocol", STD 7, RFC 793, September 1981.
